sections.h2: Who handles a Clermont County tax bill
sections.html:
The auditor values the parcel and the treasurer takes the payment, and both work out of the county building in Batavia. Call the auditor at 513-732-7150 on weekdays until 4:30 p.m. For payment questions, the treasurer's number is 513-732-7254. Look the parcel up in the auditor's property search first so you have the parcel number ready.

Batavia is the county seat and Milford is the biggest city. Villages include Bethel, Felicity, Moscow, New Richmond, Owensville and Williamsburg, plus fourteen townships. A house in West Clermont territory and one in Williamsburg can sit under very different school levies, so the parcel number matters more than the street address.

sections.h2: How the county values a house
sections.html:
The auditor sets fair market value and bills on 35% of it. Nearly 95,000 parcels sit in the county. A full reappraisal runs every six years, a midpoint update lands in between, and new construction is picked up annually.

Field appraisers drive clearly marked auditor vehicles and note additions, recent sales, damage and teardowns. A yellow door card means they stopped by and nobody answered. If you finished a basement or removed a garage, assume the change will show in the next value.

  • Value tracks the market, not the original purchase price.
  • Rates come from votes on levies, so a valuation complaint cannot lower a rate.
  • Bills run a year in arrears: what you pay in 2026 belongs to tax year 2025.

Each year has a first-half and a second-half installment, and the first half is due in February. You can pay online, by phone, by mail, or at the drop box outside 101 E. Main Street.

Section 323.12 sets December 31 and June 20 as the default dates and lets a county extend them through section 323.17. A letter counts if the U.S. Postal Service stamped it by the last day. A postage meter stamp does not count.

Under section 323.121 an unpaid installment draws a ten percent charge, cut in half when the full amount arrives within ten days. Older unpaid balances pick up interest at the rate section 5703.47 prescribes.

House Bill 186 created an inflation cap credit, and Clermont had to rebuild its second-half calculations to apply it. The school districts touched by the change are Bethel-Tate, Blanchester, Clermont Northeastern, Felicity-Franklin, Goshen, Little Miami, West Clermont, Williamsburg and Great Oaks JVS.

Owners were told they could pay first-half taxes alone, with overpayments refunded after several weeks, and lenders were asked to hold their escrow payments. For a seller the practical lesson is to get a payoff figure that reflects the credits instead of reusing last year's second-half amount.

House Bills 124, 129, 309 and 335 come with House Bill 186 in the auditor's fact sheet. They affect valuation procedure, the school 20-mill floor, budget commission oversight and inside millage, and most of their effects start with tax year 2026 bills paid in 2027.

The auditor's levy calculator multiplies the full voted millage by the tax year 2025 value. It does not apply any reduction factor the state may certify later, so treat its result as a high estimate.

Complaints against valuation are accepted from January 1 through March 31 on the Board of Revision's form. Send it electronically, mail it to 101 E. Main St., Batavia, Ohio 45103, hand it in, or email the address the auditor lists for appeals. Each owner gets one filing in a three-year stretch, and the filing opens a legal proceeding.

Revised Code 5715.19(A)(1) sets the cutoff at March 31 of the ensuing tax year or the close of first-half collection, whichever falls later. The board is the auditor as secretary, the treasurer and a commissioner, and each may send a staff member. Comparable local sales make up the best exhibit.

The board never touches a levy or a penalty. A penalty question goes to the treasurer.

sections.h2: Homestead, owner occupancy and other credits
sections.html:
Three reductions matter in a sale: Homestead, the owner occupancy credit and the one-time credit under House Bill 479.

  • Homestead: for homeowners 65 or older, for the permanently and totally disabled, and for certain surviving spouses. New applicants after January 1, 2014 must report Ohio adjusted gross income below $41,000. The deadline is December 31. An owner who is 100 percent disabled from military service can claim $56,000 where the standard figure is $28,000.
  • Owner occupancy credit: any owner who lived in the house as a primary residence on January 1 may apply, and the application often rides along with the deed.
  • One-time credit: House Bill 479 sends roughly $450 to $500 to Homestead recipients on tax year 2026 bills issued in 2027. December 31, 2026 is the last day to become eligible.

A seller who held the Homestead reduction in the current or prior tax year must file Statement of Conveyance of Homestead Property, DTE 101, with the deed. Farmland under agricultural valuation uses DTE 102.

Clermont added residents since 2020, and most households own their homes.

About 84,955 households average 2.46 people each, a steady base of family homes. Ask the auditor how the median value compares with your parcel before deciding whether a complaint is worth the effort.

Call the treasurer on 513-732-7254 for the balance by parcel number and ask whether a delinquent tax contract exists. While a valid contract stays in effect, section 323.121 stops the ten percent charge and interest from building, and a void contract revives them.

Foreclosure and tax sale auctions are listed by the sheriff on 513-732-7087, and foreclosure suits are filed through the clerk of courts, 513-732-7560. Give the title company a head start by requesting payoff letters from the treasurer and each lender early. A cash buyer can close fast, but the title company still has to pay the treasurer from your proceeds, so have the parcel number and last bill ready. Because bills run a year behind, expect the closing statement to cover the earlier tax year, and ask the title company whether the second-half amount has been recalculated for the inflation cap credit before it quotes your payoff.

faqs.q: What fraction of market value does Clermont County bill?
faqs.a: Thirty-five percent. The auditor appraises the parcel at fair market value, and the voted levies for that school district and township then apply to the 35% figure.

faqs.q: Can I protest my Clermont County valuation again next year?
faqs.a: Only once in three years. A complaint runs on a January 1 to March 31 window and speaks to value alone, not to rates or late charges.

faqs.q: Does a seller need extra forms if the house had Homestead?
faqs.a: Yes. A seller who received the Homestead reduction in the current or prior tax year files DTE 101 alongside the DTE 100 conveyance form.

faqs.q: Who answers questions about delinquent Clermont County tax?
faqs.a: The treasurer, at 513-732-7254. The auditor, at 513-732-7150, covers values, Homestead and the owner occupancy credit.

faqs.q: Is the House Bill 186 delay still affecting Clermont County bills?
faqs.a: It affected the tax year 2025 second-half bills. Ask the treasurer for the due date printed on your parcel, because revised dates were announced separately from the usual schedule.
